questions.stem: The Union Budget 2026–27 announced India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 2.0. Which combination most accurately describes its stated focus?

questions.stem: Under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which statement best describes a coastal State's exclusive economic zone (EEZ)?
options: It extends up to 200 nautical miles from the baselines, where the coastal State has specified sovereign rights over natural resources but not full territorial sovereignty
It extends exactly 200 kilometres from the coastline and gives the coastal State complete sovereignty over all navigation
It is a zone in which only the flag State of a passing vessel may exploit natural resources
It begins only beyond the continental shelf and has no fixed maximum distance
explanations: Correct — UNCLOS Part V sets an outer limit of 200 nautical miles from baselines and grants resource-related rights, not full sovereignty.
Incorrect — The distance is measured in nautical miles from baselines; an EEZ is not territorial sea.
Incorrect — Resource rights belong to the coastal State, subject to UNCLOS, not to passing vessels.
Incorrect — Article 57 specifies a maximum breadth; it is not limited to waters beyond the continental shelf.

questions.stem: A WTO member reduces the customs duty on a particular imported product from one WTO member. Subject to recognised exceptions, what does the GATT most-favoured-nation principle generally require?
options: The reduced treatment must be extended immediately and unconditionally to like products from all WTO members
The reduced treatment may be reserved permanently for the first trading partner
The reduction must apply only to products from neighbouring countries
The importing member must impose the same tariff on every product category
explanations: Correct — GATT Article I:1 generally extends an advantage to like products of all members immediately and unconditionally.
Incorrect — MFN is non-discriminatory; it does not permit a permanent preference except under recognised exceptions.
Incorrect — Geographical proximity is not the general test under Article I:1.
Incorrect — MFN concerns like products across members, not identical tariffs for unrelated product categories.

questions.stem: The LIGO observatories detect passing gravitational waves primarily by measuring:
options: A minute differential change in the lengths of two perpendicular laser-interferometer arms
A change in the chemical composition of the atmosphere above the detector
A shift in the Earth's magnetic pole measured by a compass
A change in the speed of sound through a vacuum chamber
explanations: Correct — A gravitational wave changes relative arm lengths, altering the laser-interference signal.
Incorrect — Atmospheric chemistry is not the measured signal in a laser interferometer.
Incorrect — Geomagnetic pole movement is unrelated to LIGO's measurement principle.
Incorrect — Sound cannot propagate through a vacuum; LIGO measures optical phase changes.

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.stem: In the CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing system, what is the primary role of the guide RNA?
options: It directs the Cas9 nuclease to a complementary target DNA sequence adjacent to a suitable PAM
It repairs every DNA break by independently synthesising a complete chromosome
It converts DNA directly into a protein without transcription
It prevents Cas9 from binding to any DNA sequence
explanations: Correct — The guide RNA base-pairs with the target and positions Cas9 near a compatible PAM for cleavage.
Incorrect — Cellular repair pathways repair DNA; guide RNA does not synthesise a chromosome.
Incorrect — Protein synthesis uses transcription and translation; guide RNA does not translate DNA.
Incorrect — Guide RNA provides target recognition rather than preventing target binding.

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: A river downstream of an untreated sewage discharge shows a sharp increase in biochemical oxygen demand (BOD). What does this most directly indicate?
options: A greater amount of biodegradable organic matter is available for microbial decomposition, increasing oxygen consumption
The water contains no dissolved organic matter
The river's salinity has necessarily increased
Photosynthesis has stopped permanently throughout the river basin
explanations: Correct — Microorganisms consume dissolved oxygen while decomposing biodegradable organic matter, raising BOD.
Incorrect — High BOD is associated with organic load, not its absence.
Incorrect — BOD is not a direct measure of salinity.
Incorrect — A BOD increase does not prove permanent cessation of photosynthesis.

questions.stem: A country is said to have the potential for a demographic dividend when:
options: The share of its working-age population rises relative to the dependent-age population, creating an opportunity if employment and human-capital conditions are met
Its total population increases regardless of age composition or labour-market conditions
The proportion of elderly people becomes larger than the working-age population
The birth rate becomes zero and the population immediately stops growing
explanations: Correct — A favourable age structure can lower dependency, but gains require jobs, education, health and participation.
Incorrect — Population growth alone does not establish a demographic dividend; age composition matters.
Incorrect — A larger elderly dependency burden is not the usual demographic-dividend condition.
Incorrect — Zero births would not instantly create a working-age advantage and is not the definition.

questions.stem: In the idealised global circulation model, the Coriolis force acting on moving air is:
options: Zero at the Equator and increases in magnitude towards the poles
Maximum at the Equator and zero at both poles
Equal in magnitude at every latitude
Directed vertically upward in both hemispheres
explanations: Correct — The Coriolis parameter is proportional to sin(latitude), so it is zero at the Equator and greatest at the poles.
Incorrect — This reverses the latitude dependence.
Incorrect — The Coriolis effect varies with latitude.
Incorrect — It acts horizontally and deflects motion right in the Northern Hemisphere and left in the Southern Hemisphere.
